subject: Rollover + phased-burst: proposal for auto-renew opt-out and staggered ramp
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@helixthera.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal alignment: annual to multi-year with staged-burst

Hi Markus / Camila,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday — the team had a strong reaction to Redwood's routing and burst guarantees. We are evaluating a move from a 12-month commitment to a 2-year agreement with a staged-burst ramp for production in Q4. Two asks from our side:

1) Can you propose language that allows an auto-renew but with a 60-day opt-out window tied to a usage review (we need runway for procurement approvals)?
2) We want a phased ramp schedule (Q4: +50% tokens, Q1: +100%, Q2: +150%) and a simple example showing how overages and credits would be calculated month-to-month.

Attached is our Q2 usage summary and the current PO for reference. Procurement will be looped in once we have an amendment draft.

Regards,
Sara Liu
Head of Platform Ops, Helix Therapeutics
Sara.Liu@helixthera.com
+1 415-555-0123

Attachments: usage_summary_Q2.pdf
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@helixthera.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Jul 2028 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal alignment: annual to multi-year with staged-burst

Sara — thank you, this is clear and actionable. I put together a compact amendment that addresses both asks and shows an explicit ramp / credit worked example. High level:

- Term: 24 months with an auto-renew clause that can be opted out within 60 days prior to renewal for either party; opt-out triggers a 30-day transition support window.
- Phased ramp: define three ramp bands (50%, 100%, 150%) applied to baseline committed tokens; each band has a soft overage buffer and a monthly reconciliation true-up.
- Credits & overages: provide 1:1 credit for unused committed capacity applied quarterly; overages billed at tiered usage rates with an SLO-adjusted credit for sustained latency misses.

I attached proposed_amendment_v2.pdf and a ramp table (ramp_table_q3-q5.csv) with the worked example using the Q2 numbers you sent. If procurement wants different opt-out timing or wants the opt-out tied to specific SLAs instead of a calendar window, we can adjust.

Next steps I suggest:
- You share the amendment with procurement/legal; I'll be available to walk through line items next week.
- If Helix prefers co-terming with a separate product bundle, we can draft an Appendix B with explicit burst lanes and canary capacity.

I'll follow up internally to confirm pricing at the 24-month commit and any escalation triggers.

Best,
Markus Klein
Sr. Account Lead — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

Attachments: proposed_amendment_v2.pdf; ramp_table_q3-q5.csv
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Jul 2028 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Helix — pricing decision and legal touchpoints (do not forward)

Team — quick internal note after sending the amendment to Sara. Key items we need to decide before procurement review:

- Price bands: should we hold to the current 18% effective discount for a 24-month commit, or compress to 15% if they take the Appendix B burst lanes (adds guaranteed reserved GPUs)? My preference is to keep the 18% if they accept the Appendix; otherwise move to 16% base and offer a one-time onboarding credit.
- Opt-out mechanics: 60-day calendar window is simple, but legal prefers SLA-triggered opt-out for enterprise deals. If we switch to SLA-tied opt-out, we need the exact SLO thresholds (p50/p95 latency and availability) and a remediation playbook.
- Billing reconciliation: recommend quarterly true-ups with 90-day invoice grace; procurement historically pushes for monthly reconciles, but that increases ops overhead.

I've attached the email chain below so legal can see the ask. Camila, can you confirm whether Appendix B (co-term burst lanes) needs a separate contract ID? Tessa — please weigh in on the SLO thresholds we should offer as a default (my suggestion: p95 <= 500ms, availability >= 99.9%).

Thanks,
Markus

Markus / Camila — thanks for the quick turnaround and the worked example. We reviewed internally and want to proceed to procurement with the amendment. Two small clarifications before we route: 

1) We prefer the 60-day calendar opt-out (procurement wants predictable windows).
2) Please include an explicit example of a monthly true-up when ramping from 50% to 100% in month 2 (shows overage calc + credit application).

Procurement is copied here — they'll expect a DocuSign-ready amendment and the ramp table as CSV. Can you also include the contract ID you prefer for Appendix B (if used)?

Let's target a procurement handoff demo on Thu, Jul 14 at 11:00 PT.

Sara
Head of Platform Ops, Helix Therapeutics
